title: secp256k1-ecdlp: parallel Pollard rho on 6-element classes (negation and GLV endomorphism)

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r) and Q=[x]P on secp256k1 (group order n about 2^256, cofactor 1), recover x with the randomized parallel Pollard rho algorithm with distinguished points on classes of size 6 under negation and the order-3 endomorphism (x,y)->(beta*x,y), described in proof.md. Success probability is at least 0.39 (collision of random walk points among N'=(n-1)/6 classes, 1.03 times the 0.39 point count, with disclosed walk-quality margin). Fruitless cycles of length at most 8 are detected by a fixed rule and left by an escape that depends only on the cycle (doubling its member with the smallest canonical x, canon([2]m)), so walks that merge stay merged; the escape returns to its own cycle with probability at most 2^-189.1 (random-mapping model), and its batched doubling is charged. Total work is at most 2^127.47 target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing (2^32.01), walk steps at one reference operation plus 650 charged instructions for canonicalisation, cycle test, distinguished-point test and bookkeeping (C=1000), distinguished-point detection delay (theta=2^-56), cycle detection, cycle walk and the charged doubling escape, unrecognised-cycle waste, storage and lookup, walk starts, scalar recovery and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^76.6 bytes; nonuniform advice is 2^0 bytes. Classical, no quantum steps. Heuristics: random-walk behaviour of a 2^20-entry additive table walk on classes (Teske 2001, van Oorschot-Wiener 1999) within 5.7 percent in collision rate, the stated cycle rates, and per-step instruction counts that are stated bounds, not measurements. This is an analytic accounting claim, not a practical attack.

experiments.purpose: Run the class-6 distinguished-point rho end to end on a toy curve of prime order 523969 with an order-3 endomorphism, check scalar recovery, count how often the doubling escape re-enters its cycle (against a table-step escape control), and check that a second walker restarted from a random point of a first walker's trail (empty history, possibly inside a cycle) reaches the same distinguished point. Toy scope only; does not establish production cost or walk quality.
